hooks: You know what runs your code. How do objects prove they are equal, and why does it matter?
Equality is defined. How do collections use it to store and find things?
Collections hold objects. How does the compiler keep their types safe?
Types are safe. How do you process these collections in a modern style?
Streams read well. How do you design the types they work on, with interfaces or abstract classes?
The design is set. What happens when something goes wrong?
Errors are handled. How do you run all of this on many threads?
java-core.upNext: Core Java is covered. Next: what the JVM does with your code, memory, garbage collection and tuning.

hooks: You know where objects live. How does the collector decide what to clean up?
Garbage is collected. Classes have to get into memory first, so how are they found?
Classes load. When memory runs out anyway, how do you find the cause?
Memory errors are diagnosed. What if the CPU is pinned instead?
The hot code is found. Why is the app slow right after it starts?
The JIT warms up. How does the JVM behave inside a container?
Limits are respected. Which flags do you actually set in production?
jvm.upNext: JVM internals are covered. Next: Spring, the framework that runs on top of all this.

hooks: Spring wires objects for you. What does Boot configure on top of that?
Boot sets things up. How do you expose it as a REST API?
The API takes requests. How does the data get stored and read?
Repositories save entities. When do several saves have to succeed together?
Transactions protect data. Who is allowed to call all this?
Security is in place. How do you see what is happening in production?
You can observe it. How do you prove it all works before release?
spring.upNext: Spring is covered. Next: how Maven and Gradle build and package it into something deployable.

hooks: The POM describes the project. What do the lifecycle phases do with it?
You know the phases. Which libraries come along, and with what scope?
Transitive jars pile up. What happens when two versions of one clash?
Conflicts are resolved. How does Gradle model the same problem differently?
You know both tools. How do you split a big project into modules?
Modules build together. How do you make the output identical every time?
Builds are reproducible. How do you know your dependencies are safe?
java-build.upNext: Builds are clear. Next: the same ideas in other ecosystems, or deploy what you built.
